A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiT, PixArt, and MMDiT training and hyperparameter-search results, including a human text-image alignment evaluation, in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds MMDiT GenEval scores and an output-multiplier analysis across batch sizes.

M1.justification: The parameterization rules, architecture adaptations, initialization, head-count scaling, and µTransfer algorithms remain unchanged. Expanded motivation and explanations of hyperparameter selection do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The represented datasets and tasks remain unchanged: ImageNet class-to-image generation and text-to-image experiments using SA-1B, the internal corpus, MJHQ, MS-COCO, GenEval, and internal prompts. Applying GenEval to MMDiT extends evaluation of a retained architecture without introducing new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The original DiT, PixArt-α, and human-tuned MMDiT-18B baselines remain. The new GenEval comparison uses the same MMDiT pair. AuraFlow is added to the discussion but is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: v2 adds GenEval scoring to the MMDiT-18B evaluation and an output-multiplier sweep across batch sizes 128, 256, and 512 at width 288 and 200K training steps. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged; the additional guidance specifications are disclosures.

E4.justification: v1 tests output-multiplier transfer across widths and training steps. v2 extends this sensitivity analysis to batch sizes in Appendix E.2.2, Figure 7(b), and Table 12. Other supplementary checks and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests. Seed and repeated-run reporting remain unchanged, and the added tables introduce no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports MMDiT GenEval overall scores of 0.8218 for µP and 0.8154 for the baseline, with mixed subcategory outcomes, including lower counting performance for µP (79.69 versus 81.88). Table 12 adds output-multiplier results across batch sizes. Matched DiT, PixArt, and human-evaluation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1, the scaling rules, Assumption C.1, and the Appendix C derivations remain unchanged. v2 explains the previously asserted generalization to finite fixed dimensions and nonuniform widths more explicitly, without adding or revising a proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same theoretical-equivalence and hyperparameter-transfer contributions, including 2.9× DiT convergence acceleration and the 5.5% and 3% tuning-cost claims. Additional evidence supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving gradient noise, flatter minima, conservative single-epoch training, and improved PixArt generalization. It recommends matching classifier-free guidance between proxy and target evaluations and expands future directions. The unresolved optimal-proxy-size limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 specifies PixArt classifier-free guidance of 4.5, clarifies unguided DiT evaluation, and explains MMDiT hyperparameter selection using the training-loss envelope. These improve documentation; hardware costs, code-access information, and asset licenses are retained.

R1.justification: v2 identifies AuraFlow v0.1 as the closest prior work and distinguishes its empirical application from this paper's proofs, systematic transfer tests, and 18B scaling. It also adds background and future-work citations, including Muon and SDXL, while retaining the existing related-work survey.

P1.justification: v2 expands several explanations, introduces a separate Discussion section before the retained Conclusion, and updates acknowledgments and front-page information. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4 and 12 and a batch-size panel to Figure 7, with corresponding display relocations. Figure 6's caption changes 50K to 15K steps, matching the finding already in v1 Appendix E.4.4. Existing plots and qualitative examples otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens validation through MMDiT GenEval results and the additional batch-size sensitivity analysis. Clearer guidance and selection details improve reproducibility, while acknowledging AuraFlow improves research positioning. The new GenEval advantage is small and mixed across subtasks, without uncertainty estimates; the gains in paper quality are useful but limited.
